# `Q-5-16` — `resources:` Pattern Matched No Files

> A `resources:` glob matched no files, so nothing was published
> for it.

## What this means

Each `resources:` entry names files to copy into the output
directory alongside the rendered site. This warning fires when a
glob entry matched nothing at all — the rest of the resource list
is unaffected, so the render continues without whatever that
pattern was meant to publish.

Only *glob* entries produce this warning. A literal path that does
not exist is reported by name instead (see `Q-5-6`), which is the
more useful message when there is a single file to point at.

## Why this happens

The most common cause is a pattern written for Quarto 1. In
Quarto 2, `*` matches within **one** directory level:

```yaml
resources:
  - "data/*.csv"        # CSVs directly in data/
  - "data/**/*.csv"     # CSVs anywhere under data/
  - data                # everything under data/
```

Other causes:

- **A typo** in a directory or file name.
- **The pattern resolves against a different directory than you
  expect.** A `resources:` entry resolves relative to the file it
  is written in: document front matter → that document's
  directory, `_metadata.yml` → that file's directory,
  `_quarto.yml` → the project root. A leading `/` always anchors
  at the project root.

## How to fix

Check the pattern against the project layout, and add `**/` if you
meant to search subdirectories. To publish a whole directory, name
it:

```yaml
resources:
  - data
```
